unit.label: Landlords, repairs & natural speech
unit.title: Settling Into the New Place
unit.description: Cover this lesson the conversation through the landlord phone call: already/getting used to, household problems, waiting and appointments, repairs and payment, existential subjects with 有, the likelihood use of 會, and natural omission of understood subjects and objects.

goal.text: 熱水器的水好像不熱。今天我會去看看。
goal.pinyin: Rèshuǐqì de shuǐ hǎoxiàng bú rè. Jīntiān wǒ huì qù kànkan.
goal.meaning: The water from the water heater doesn't seem hot. I'll go take a look today.

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 11 Dialogue II / Vocabulary II (printed pp. 227–229) and Grammar III–V (printed pp. 232–235). The source-listed 等 is taught formally; 那 'then/in that case', 不好意思, 房租, and 得 děi are retained explicitly in dialogue-based teaching rather than omitted.

lessons.title: Call the Landlord
lessons.subtitle: Open the landlord phone call with 喂, 收到, and the rent-payment phrase 房租.

steps.prompt: In 你收到我的房租了嗎？, what does 房租 mean?
options: rent for a room or house
a room that is for rent
steps.answer: rent for a room or house
steps.explanation: 房租 is the rent payment. Compare 租房, which means to rent a place.

lessons.title: Already Settled In
lessons.subtitle: Use 已經, 習慣, and 問題 to report how the new place is going.

options: get used to; be accustomed to
steps.answer: get used to; be accustomed to
steps.explanation: 習慣 is to get used to or be accustomed to something.

lessons.title: The Water Doesn't Seem Hot
lessons.subtitle: Use 熱水器 and the softening expression 好像.

steps.prompt: What does 好像 do in the complaint?
steps.explanation: 好像 expresses an appearance or impression and often softens a comment.

steps.prompt: Which item is a water heater?
steps.explanation: 熱水器 is a water heater.

lessons.title: Install It, but Pay Yourself
lessons.subtitle: Ask for cable TV, then use 不過 to introduce the landlord's condition.

steps.prompt: In 不過你得自己付錢, how is 得 read and what does it mean?
steps.explanation: the conversation uses 得 děi as 'must / have to.' This is a different pronunciation and function from 得 de after a verb.

lessons.title: Someone Lives Here
lessons.subtitle: Respond politely with 沒關係, then learn why an indefinite subject is introduced with 有.

steps.prompt: How do you negate existential 有 in 'no one lives here'?
steps.explanation: Existential 有 is negated with 沒有.

lessons.title: Will It Happen? Say Only What You Need
lessons.subtitle: Distinguish the two 會 meanings, use 那 as 'then/in that case,' and omit recoverable subjects or objects.

steps.prompt: In 明天我會去看看, what kind of 會 is this?
steps.explanation: The future time expression and event reading point to likelihood.

steps.prompt: In 朋友給我一個西瓜，我不想吃, what is omitted after 吃?
steps.explanation: The object 西瓜 was just mentioned and is recoverable.

lessons.title: Unit 33 Review
lessons.subtitle: Phone calls with the landlord, settling in, problems and repairs, indefinite subjects, two kinds of 會, and natural omission.

steps.prompt: Which phone greeting is used here?
You need to apologize politely before explaining a conflict. Which phrase fits?
steps.explanation: 不好意思 is the apology/excuse; 沒關係 is a response meaning 'no problem.'

steps.prompt: The rule here contrasts 地上有一支手機 with 有一支手機在地上. Which one puts the location 地上 in focus?
steps.explanation: Both describe a cellphone on the floor, but the rule here says 有一支手機在地上 puts the location 地上 in focus; 地上有一支手機 focuses the new cellphone information.

steps.prompt: Which 不會 is the this lesson future-likelihood use rather than 'doesn't know how'?
options: 他明天不會去上書法課。
steps.answer: 他明天不會去上書法課。
steps.explanation: 明天 + 不會 + future event gives the likelihood/won't reading. 我不會打籃球 is the acquired-skill meaning: I don't know how to play basketball.

steps.prompt: At the door, the landlord says 請進！ Which subject is understood but not spoken?
steps.explanation: The listener is the understood subject: (你)請進. This is the rule here context-predictable zero-pronoun case.

steps.prompt: Listen for what has already happened.

steps.explanation: 等 děng means to wait for.

喂.note: 喂 is fourth-tone wèi here, the conventional way to answer or address someone on the phone.
喂.memory: 口 is a compact three-stroke block on the left; 畏 fills the taller right side.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 口.

parts.label: 畏
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final nine strokes form 畏 on the right.

收.note: 收 is first-tone shōu. In 收到, it combines with 到 to mean receive.
收.memory: The two-stroke left shape stays narrow; 攵 uses four active strokes on the right.

parts.label: 丩
parts.name: left shape
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow left group.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: action component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 攵.

已.note: 已 is third-tone yǐ. It is the first character of 已經, “already.”
已.memory: 已 is a compact three-stroke bent shape. Keep the final rising stroke inside the upper bend rather than closing a box.

parts.label: 已
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: All three strokes form one compact bent character.

經.meaning: pass through; second character of 已經
經.note: 經 is first-tone jīng. In 已經 it completes the fixed adverb meaning “already.”
經.memory: 糹 forms six thread strokes on the left; 巠 forms the seven-stroke right block.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 糹.

parts.label: 巠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form 巠.

習.note: 習 is second-tone xí. In 習慣 it is part of the verb “to get used to; be accustomed to.”
習.memory: 羽 forms two wing-like groups across the top; 白 is the five-stroke block underneath.

parts.label: 羽
parts.name: feather component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 羽.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: white component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 白.

慣.meaning: accustomed; second character of 習慣
慣.note: 慣 is fourth-tone guàn. Learn 習慣 as the complete word “to get used to; be accustomed to.”
慣.memory: 忄 supplies three narrow heart strokes on the left; 貫 fills the denser eleven-stroke right side.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 忄.

parts.label: 貫
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final eleven strokes form 貫.

器.note: 器 is fourth-tone qì. In 熱水器 it means an appliance or device: a water heater.
器.memory: Four 口 boxes surround 犬 in the middle. Keep the top pair and bottom pair balanced around the central four strokes.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: upper-left mouth
parts.description: The first three strokes form the upper-left 口.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: upper-right mouth
parts.description: The next three strokes form the upper-right 口.

parts.label: 犬
parts.name: central component
parts.description: Four strokes form 犬 in the middle.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: lower-left mouth
parts.description: The next three strokes form the lower-left 口.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: lower-right mouth
parts.description: The final three strokes form the lower-right 口.

像.note: 像 is fourth-tone xiàng. In 好像 it helps express “seem; appear to be,” often softening a comment.
像.memory: 亻 + 象: a narrow person component beside the full twelve-stroke 象 shape.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow 亻 on the left.

parts.label: 象
parts.name: elephant component
parts.description: The remaining twelve strokes form 象 on the right; keep its stacked turns and lower sweeping strokes open and balanced.

裝.note: 裝 is first-tone zhuāng. In the rental conversation it is the verb “to install,” as in installing cable TV.
裝.memory: 壯 forms the seven-stroke upper block; 衣 supplies the six lower strokes.

parts.label: 壯
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 壯.

parts.label: 衣
parts.name: clothing component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 衣.

過.note: 過 is fourth-tone guò. Here it appears inside 不過, “however/but”; that use is different from the later direction verb 過 “go past.”
過.memory: Build the nine-stroke 咼 first; then add the four-stroke movement component 辶, whose final sweep runs underneath.

parts.name: inner component

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 辶 and sweep under the inner block.

付.note: 付 is fourth-tone fù. In this lesson it means to pay money.
付.memory: 亻 takes two strokes on the left; 寸 uses the final three strokes on the right.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亻.

parts.label: 寸
parts.name: inch component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 寸.

關.note: 關 is first-tone guān. In 沒關係, the whole expression means “it doesn't matter / no problem.”
關.memory: The eight-stroke 門 creates the outer door frame; the remaining eleven strokes form the compact inner structure.

parts.label: inner

係.note: 係 is fourth-tone xì. It is the final character of 沒關係.
係.memory: 亻 is the two-stroke left component; 系 supplies the seven-stroke right side.

parts.label: 系

線.memory: 糹 makes the six-stroke thread component on the left; 泉 makes the nine-stroke right block.

parts.label: 泉

u33-existential-you.title: Introduce an indefinite subject with 有
u33-existential-you.explanation: 有 introduces the existence of an indefinite subject, and the following VP says what that subject does: 有人住這裡, 有兩個學生來找你. Because a bare subject is normally definite, a new indefinite subject is introduced with 有. Existential 有 is always negated with 沒有. The rule here also contrasts 地上有一支手機 with 有一支手機在地上: the basic existence is similar, but the first puts the new cellphone information in focus, while the second makes the location 地上 the focus.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu liǎng ge xuéshēng lái zhǎo nǐ.
examples.meaning: Two students came to look for you.
No one lives in this room.
There is a cellphone on the floor.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu yì zhī shǒujī zài dìshang.
examples.meaning: There is a cellphone on the floor.

u33-existential-you.remember: Use 有 before a new indefinite subject and 沒有 for its negative. Word order can shift the information focus even when the existence meaning stays similar.

u33-hui-likelihood.title: 會: learned skill or likelihood?
u33-hui-likelihood.explanation: The rule here distinguishes two uses of 會. The earlier 會 means an acquired skill: 他會做飯, 'he knows how to cook.' this lesson adds 會 for possibility or likelihood, commonly about a future event: 我明天會去看看他. Context—not the character alone—determines the reading. 不會 likewise can mean either 'doesn't know how' or 'will probably not / won't.'

examples.meaning: I don't know how to play basketball.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kànkan tā.
examples.meaning: I'll probably go see him tomorrow.

examples.text: 他明天不會去上書法課。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngtiān bú huì qù shàng shūfǎkè.
examples.meaning: He won't / probably won't go to calligraphy class tomorrow.

u33-hui-likelihood.remember: With a learned activity, 會 can mean know how. With a future event, 會 can mean will / be likely to. Read the whole context.

u33-zero-pronoun.title: Leave understood subjects and objects unspoken
u33-zero-pronoun.explanation: Chinese often omits old information when the listener can recover it from the immediate situation or from an earlier mention. The rule here calls an omitted pronoun a zero pronoun. The most frequent omissions are subjects and objects: a subject can be understood from context even without being spoken (請進! has an understood 你), a previously mentioned subject can disappear in the next clause, and a previously mentioned object can be left unspoken. Keep the noun or pronoun whenever omission would make the meaning ambiguous.

examples.text: 我常打籃球，也常踢足球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cháng dǎ lánqiú, yě cháng tī zúqiú.
examples.meaning: I often play basketball, and also often play soccer.

examples.text: 朋友給我一個西瓜，我不想吃。
examples.pinyin: Péngyǒu gěi wǒ yí ge xīguā, wǒ bù xiǎng chī.
examples.meaning: A friend gave me a watermelon; I don't want to eat it.

u33-zero-pronoun.remember: If the listener already knows who or what you mean, Chinese often says less. Context-predictable subjects, repeated subjects, and repeated objects can all be omitted when the referent stays clear.

u33-phone.note: 喂 is the conventional phone greeting in this context.

u33-received.meaning: I have already received the rent.
u33-received.note: 房租 is the rent payment for a room or house; 收到 means receive. Compare 租房, which means to rent a place.

u33-habit.meaning: I have already gotten used to it.
u33-habit.note: 習慣 describes becoming accustomed to a situation.

u33-problem.note: 問題 is problem or question.

u33-heater.pinyin: Rèshuǐqì de shuǐ hǎoxiàng bú rè.
u33-heater.meaning: The water from the water heater doesn't seem hot.
u33-heater.note: 好像 often softens a comment: it seems/apparently.

u33-will-check.meaning: I'll go take a look today.
u33-will-check.note: With a future time and action, 會 expresses likelihood/will, not an acquired skill.

u33-sorry.text: 不好意思，今天晚上我有事。
u33-sorry.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, jīntiān wǎnshang wǒ yǒu shì.
u33-sorry.meaning: Sorry, I have something to do tonight.
u33-sorry.note: 不好意思 is the listed polite apology/excuse used before the scheduling conflict; it is now indexed explicitly as vocabulary.

u33-no-problem.note: 沒關係 is the standard response meaning it doesn't matter / no problem.

u33-then.text: 那我明天下午兩點到。還有問題嗎？
u33-then.pinyin: Nà wǒ míngtiān xiàwǔ liǎng diǎn dào. Hái yǒu wèntí ma?
u33-then.meaning: Then I'll arrive at two tomorrow afternoon. Are there any other problems?
u33-then.note: Here 那 is the discourse particle 'then / in that case.' 還有問題嗎 asks whether there are any additional problems.

u33-install.text: 我想買電視。請問可以幫我裝有線電視嗎？
u33-install.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi diànshì. Qǐngwèn kěyǐ bāng wǒ zhuāng yǒuxiàn diànshì ma?
u33-install.meaning: I want to buy a television. Could you help me install cable TV?
u33-install.note: This follows the request sequence in the conversation: buying a TV, then asking the landlord to install cable.

u33-pay.text: 可以，不過你得自己付錢。
u33-pay.pinyin: Kěyǐ, búguò nǐ děi zìjǐ fù qián.
u33-pay.meaning: Yes, but you have to pay for it yourself.
u33-pay.note: Here 得 is read děi and means 'must / have to,' distinct from the earlier complement marker 得 de.

u33-exist.note: 有 introduces the indefinite subject 人 before the verb.

u33-noexist.meaning: No one lives in this room.
u33-noexist.note: Existential 有 is negated with 沒有.

u33-location-exist.pinyin: Yǒu yí ge rén zài zhèlǐ.
u33-location-exist.note: 有 + indefinite NP introduces the person before stating the location.

u33-omit-subject.text: 我常打籃球，也常踢足球。
u33-omit-subject.pinyin: Wǒ cháng dǎ lánqiú, yě cháng tī zúqiú.
u33-omit-subject.meaning: I often play basketball, and also often play soccer.
u33-omit-subject.note: Following the rule here pattern, the second clause omits the already-mentioned subject 我.

u33-omit-object.text: 朋友給我一個西瓜，我不想吃。
u33-omit-object.pinyin: Péngyǒu gěi wǒ yí ge xīguā, wǒ bù xiǎng chī.
u33-omit-object.meaning: A friend gave me a watermelon; I don't want to eat it.
u33-omit-object.note: The object 西瓜 is recoverable, so the second clause omits it.

u33-wait.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ zài jiā děng nǐ.
u33-wait.meaning: Okay, I'll wait for you at home.
u33-wait.note: 等 děng is the lesson verb 'to wait for.'

u33-rent-question.pinyin: Nǐ shōudào wǒ de fángzū le ma?
u33-rent-question.note: This preserves the opening question of the conversation; 房租 is the rent paid for a room or house.

u33-time.text: 你什麼時候有空？晚上可以嗎？
u33-time.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou yǒu kòng? Wǎnshang kěyǐ ma?
u33-time.meaning: When are you free? Would tonight be okay?
u33-time.note: The landlord uses familiar scheduling language before arranging the repair visit.
